newsitem.title: CHINA: China, ASEAN seek talks on territorial disputes.
newsitem.headline: China, ASEAN seek talks on territorial disputes.

text.p: China and the members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) agreed on Friday to tackle their terroritorial disputes through talks and to prevent differences hampering normal relations.

The two days of political talks between China and the ASEAN nations -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- was the third such meeting and the first since ASEAN granted China full-dialogue status last July.

On Friday, Beijing reiterated its position on the existing differences concerning borders and territories between China and some ASEAN nations, the Xinhua news agency quoted Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Tang Jiaxuan as saying after the talks.
China has longstanding territorial differences with several ASEAN members over its claims to the Spratly islands in the South China Sea.

Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam also claim the islands, and have been disturbed by what they have seen as China's increasingly blatant forays to claim the archipelago of coral reefs and atolls that are believed rich in oil.
"The two sides expressed the will to maintain regional peace and stability," Tang was quoted as saying.

"It is imperative to handle differences through negotiations in order to seek a proper settlement, (and) not allow the differences to interfere in the normal development of relations between countries," Tang said.
